criteria.name: regex_anchored_line_start

criteria.name: inline_sprint_references_not_counted

criteria.name: log_filename_timestamp_format
criteria.description: All conversation log filenames are prefixed with a timestamp matching the pattern YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS- (e.g., '2026.04.12-14.30.00-sprint-2-attempt-0-generator.md').

criteria.name: resume_does_not_overwrite_logs
criteria.description: When the harness resumes and re-runs the same sprint/attempt, a new log file is created with a different timestamp prefix; the original log file from the prior run remains on disk and is not overwritten or deleted.

criteria.name: contract_negotiation_logs_timestamped
criteria.description: Contract negotiation conversation logs follow the timestamped naming pattern (e.g., 'YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS-sprint-3-contract-negotiation.md').

criteria.name: all_agent_log_types_timestamped
criteria.description: Generator, Evaluator, Planner, and Documenter conversation logs all use the timestamp prefix format — no log file in .adhd/logs/ is written without a timestamp prefix.

criteria.name: timestamp_uses_configured_timezone
criteria.description: The timestamp in log filenames reflects the configured timezone (not UTC by default unless configured as UTC), consistent with the HH:MM:SS timestamps used in terminal output.

criteria.name: langfuse_span_names_aligned
criteria.description: Langfuse trace span names for agent conversations include the same timestamped identifier used in the log filename, enabling cross-referencing between log files and trace spans.

criteria.name: regex_fix_has_test_coverage
criteria.description: There is at least one test file covering the sprint-counting regex that tests: (1) standard headings are counted, (2) inline prose references are not counted, and (3) blockquoted or indented heading-like lines are not counted.

criteria.name: existing_contract_reused_on_resume
criteria.description: When the harness runs with --resume and `.adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json` already exists on disk, it loads and uses that contract without invoking contract negotiation agents (no Planner/Evaluator calls for that sprint's contract).

criteria.name: missing_contract_triggers_negotiation
criteria.description: When the harness runs with --resume and `.adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json` does NOT exist on disk, contract negotiation proceeds normally as if it were a fresh run.

criteria.name: loaded_contract_logged
criteria.description: When an existing contract is loaded from disk during resume, a log message is emitted that includes both the fact it was loaded from disk and the number of criteria in the contract (e.g., 'Loaded contract from disk for sprint 2 with 8 criteria').

criteria.name: contract_file_validation
criteria.description: When loading a contract from disk, the code validates that the file contains well-formed JSON matching the expected contract structure before using it. Malformed or empty contract files trigger negotiation rather than crashing.

criteria.name: parse_failure_writes_diagnostic_file
criteria.description: When parseContract fails to extract valid JSON from the evaluator's contract review response, a file `.adhd/logs/sprint-N-contract-parse-error.txt` is created containing the full raw unparseable text.

criteria.name: parse_failure_logs_truncated_preview
criteria.description: When parseContract falls back to the default contract due to a parse failure, a warning is logged to the console containing a truncated preview of the raw text (not the full 2000+ character blob).

criteria.name: successful_parse_no_diagnostic_file
criteria.description: When parseContract successfully extracts valid contract JSON, no `.adhd/logs/sprint-N-contract-parse-error.txt` file is created.

criteria.name: diagnostic_directory_created_on_demand
criteria.description: If `.adhd/logs/` does not exist when a parse error diagnostic needs to be written, the directory is created automatically (no crash on missing directory).

criteria.name: truncation_length_reasonable
criteria.description: The truncated preview logged to console on parse failure is capped at a reasonable length (200-500 characters) with an ellipsis or indicator showing it was truncated, so console output stays readable.

criteria.name: adhd_artifacts_committed_before_generator
criteria.description: Before each Generator agent invocation, all pending .adhd/ files (contracts, progress, feedback) are staged and committed with a commit message prefixed by '[adhd]'. The Generator starts with no uncommitted .adhd/ files in the working tree.

criteria.name: adhd_commit_message_format
criteria.description: The commit created for .adhd/ artifacts uses a message starting with '[adhd]' and includes the sprint number (e.g., '[adhd] Sprint 2: artifacts').

criteria.name: clean_working_tree_for_generator

criteria.name: revert_uses_git_reset_hard

criteria.name: adhd_files_survive_revert
criteria.description: When revertToCheckpoint resets to a checkpoint SHA, .adhd/ files (progress.json, contracts/, feedback/) that were written after the checkpoint are preserved by stashing before reset and unstashing after. The files exist on disk with their pre-revert contents after the operation completes.

criteria.name: stash_unstash_error_handling
criteria.description: If git stash or unstash fails during revertToCheckpoint, the error is logged with a meaningful message and does not cause an unhandled exception. The revert still completes (reset --hard succeeds) even if stash restoration fails.

criteria.name: documenting_status_type

criteria.name: documenting_status_set_before_documenter

criteria.name: complete_status_after_documenter

criteria.name: no_regression_on_existing_revert_callers

criteria.name: commit_is_noop_when_no_changes

criteria.name: terminal_bell_at_hitl_gates

criteria.name: terminal_bell_on_fatal_error

criteria.name: notify_flag_parsed

criteria.name: desktop_notification_with_notify_flag

criteria.name: no_desktop_notification_without_flag

criteria.name: commit_adhd_flag_parsed

criteria.name: commit_adhd_creates_metadata_commit

criteria.name: commit_adhd_logs_includes_logs

criteria.name: commit_adhd_logs_implies_commit_adhd

criteria.name: default_no_adhd_commits

criteria.name: app_starts_and_parses_new_flags

criteria.name: e2e_phantom_sprint_prevention

criteria.name: e2e_commit_adhd_flags
criteria.description: Running with --commit-adhd produces [adhd] commits containing contracts/feedback/progress/spec after each sprint, and --commit-adhd-logs additionally includes .adhd/logs/. Running without either flag produces no [adhd] metadata commits

criteria.name: e2e_notifications

criteria.name: progress_status_lifecycle

criteria.name: contract_parse_error_diagnostics

criteria.name: timestamp_log_consistency
criteria.description: All conversation log files (generator, evaluator, contract negotiation, documenter) use YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS prefix format. Multiple runs for the same sprint produce distinct timestamped files, and chronological ls ordering matches execution order

criteria.name: clean_working_tree_before_generator
criteria.description: Immediately before every Generator invocation, git status --porcelain shows no uncommitted .adhd/ files — they have been committed with an [adhd] prefix message

criteria.name: readme_cli_flags_documented
criteria.description: README or equivalent documentation describes --resume, --notify, --commit-adhd, and --commit-adhd-logs flags with usage examples and explains their interaction (e.g., --commit-adhd-logs implies --commit-adhd)

criteria.name: stage_usage_model_field_stored_exactly
criteria.description: When `recordStage` is called with a model string (e.g. `"claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`), the resulting `StageUsage` entry in tracker state has `model` equal to that exact string — no truncation, no transformation.

criteria.name: record_stage_model_parameter_required

criteria.name: shared_has_zero_llm_sdk_imports
criteria.description: A grep of all files under `shared/` for LLM-SDK import strings (e.g. `@anthropic-ai/`, `@ai-sdk/`, `openai`) returns zero matches after this sprint's changes are applied.

criteria.name: call_site_model_routing_correct

criteria.name: per_stage_summary_includes_model_column
criteria.description: The per-stage formatting pure helper, when invoked with a sample `StageUsage[]` containing at least two distinct models, returns strings where each row contains the stage's `model` value as a left-aligned text column immediately after the stage name and before the numeric columns. Asserted directly on returned `string[]` without log capture.

criteria.name: per_model_rollup_aggregation_correct
criteria.description: The pure rollup aggregator, when given `StageUsage[]` where model `"X"` appears in three stages with (inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 50, costUsd: 0.01), (200, 80, 0.02), (300, 120, 0.03), returns a `ModelRollupRow` for `"X"` with inputTokens=600, outputTokens=250, costUsd=0.06. Asserted directly on the returned struct.

criteria.name: per_model_rollup_sorted_by_usd_descending
criteria.description: When the rollup aggregator is given stages across three models with total USD of 0.05, 0.20, and 0.10, the returned `ModelRollupRow[]` is ordered: 0.20, 0.10, 0.05. The terminal summary renders them in this order.

criteria.name: rollup_always_printed_even_single_model

criteria.name: legacy_usage_json_loads_without_throw

A subsequent `save()` rewrites the file with `model: "unknown"` on all legacy entries and the new model string on any newly-recorded entries.

criteria.name: save_load_round_trip_preserves_model
criteria.description: A tracker that records stages with models `"alpha"`, `"beta"`, and `"gamma"`, calls `save()`, then is replaced by a fresh tracker instance that loads the same file: every stage's `model` in the loaded state equals the originally-recorded string. No model value is lost, coerced, or defaulted to `"unknown"`.

criteria.name: usage_json_key_order_consistent
criteria.description: Each stage object in a freshly-written `.adhd/usage.json` has keys in the order: `stage`, `model`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `costUsd`, `durationMs`. Verified by reading the raw JSON string and checking key insertion order on at least one stage entry.

criteria.name: typecheck_and_lint_pass_clean
criteria.description: `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` (Biome) both exit with code 0 after all sprint changes. Zero new `any` casts are introduced in `shared/` or `harness-claude/` files touched by this sprint.

criteria.name: documentation_files_updated_correctly
criteria.description: README.md contains updated Cost tracking paragraph and Observability bullet mentioning per-model attribution. docs/INTERNALS.md Cost Tracking section describes both summary views and the persisted `model` field. docs/ROADMAP.md Part 1 §1.11 bullet 3 is extended; Parts 2 and 3 contain no new per-model tracking entry. CHANGELOG.md contains a new `## Phase 1.6: Observability Sharpening` section with `### Sprint 1 -- Per-Model Usage Tracking` immediately after the Phase 1.5 block, using identical heading levels and Features→bullets→Verified line ordering.

criteria.name: surfaces_round_trip
criteria.description: Writing a negotiated contract with surfaces to .adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json and re-reading it yields the identical surfaces array (same values, same membership, same order), with stable key ordering in the persisted JSON matching existing conventions.

criteria.name: legacy_contract_loads
criteria.description: Parsing a legacy contract JSON that has no surfaces field succeeds without throwing; the absent field is treated as unspecified (empty or undefined surface list), never crashing the run, and re-persisting it does not inject spurious values.

criteria.name: proposer_emits_surfaces
criteria.description: After contract negotiation runs, the resulting contract contains a non-empty surfaces array drawn only from the allowed vocabulary, reflecting the sprint's footprint. The proposer prompt explicitly instructs use of only the allowed vocabulary.

criteria.name: reviewer_validates_surfaces
criteria.description: Given a candidate contract whose surfaces is missing, empty, or contains an unknown token, the reviewer step produces an approved contract whose surfaces is present, non-empty, and contains only allowed vocabulary values: unknown tokens are dropped, and a contract that would end up with an empty surfaces list is rejected rather than approved.

criteria.name: app_starts_and_tests_pass
criteria.description: bun run typecheck, bun run lint, and bun test all pass cleanly. The harness still starts and negotiates a contract end-to-end without regressions to existing contract persistence.

criteria.name: graceful_degradation_no_crash
criteria.description: Model/tier resolution never throws and never crashes a run on odd input (missing env vars, empty/whitespace-only strings, unknown model overrides, mixed-case env values); it always produces concrete non-empty resolved model strings, consistent with the project's graceful-degradation convention. An unknown explicit override is passed through (or mapped) rather than causing an exception.

criteria.name: classifier_lives_in_surfaces_module
criteria.description: The new classification function is added to and exported from the existing shared/surfaces.ts module (no new parallel surface module is created), and it reuses the already-defined SURFACE_VOCABULARY, Surface type, and isSurface rather than redefining them.

criteria.name: returns_deduplicated_surface_set
criteria.description: Given a list of file path strings, the function returns the deduplicated set of Surface values touched. Backend source paths plus a test path classify to exactly {backend, tests}; frontend UI files plus a markdown file classify to exactly {frontend, docs}; duplicate paths or multiple paths of the same surface yield a single entry.

criteria.name: covers_all_six_surfaces
criteria.description: Default patterns correctly classify representative paths for every vocabulary token: db (migrations/schema/seed files), config (package manifests, lockfiles, dotfiles, CI config), tests (test directories or test-named files), frontend (.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.css and client UI dirs), backend (server-side source not frontend/tests), and docs (markdown/documentation). Covers both TS/Node and Python/Go style paths.

criteria.name: documented_single_surface_precedence
criteria.description: Each path maps to at most one surface via an explicit, documented evaluation order. A test file with a frontend extension (e.g. a .test.tsx file) resolves to tests only, not frontend, and this precedence is verified by a test.

criteria.name: deterministic_order_independent
criteria.description: Classifying the same path list in different orders yields an identical resulting set; results are deterministic across repeated calls with no dependence on input ordering.

criteria.name: never_throws_on_odd_input
criteria.description: The function never throws on degenerate input — empty path list returns an empty set; empty strings, whitespace, paths with no extension, and unrecognized paths are silently omitted from the result rather than causing an error (mirroring normalizeSurfaces' best-effort contract).

criteria.name: purity_no_io_or_sdk
criteria.description: The function performs no git, filesystem, or network calls and has no side effects — it operates solely on the provided path strings. shared/surfaces.ts contains zero Claude SDK imports, preserving the shared/ boundary.

criteria.name: full_unit_test_coverage

criteria.name: clean_typecheck_lint_build
criteria.description: `bun run typecheck` reports no errors, `bun run lint` passes with no new violations, and the full `bun test` suite (including pre-existing Sprint 1 tests) passes — the module integrates cleanly with the existing codebase end-to-end.

criteria.name: changed_files_helper_returns_paths

criteria.name: evaluator_skipped_no_cost_on_failure

criteria.name: coverage_pass_runs_evaluator

criteria.name: retry_feedback_propagates_missed_surface

criteria.name: skip_when_no_declared_surfaces_or_no_diff

criteria.name: clean_build_and_tests

criteria.name: named_tier_constants_replace_stale_default
criteria.description: Model IDs are defined once as named tier constants (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a single place (shared/models.ts or a delineated block in shared/config.ts) using current generally-available model IDs. criteria.name: per_agent_default_matrix

criteria.name: resolution_precedence_per_agent
criteria.description: Precedence is enforced per agent: an explicit --model-<agent>/MODEL_<AGENT> override wins over an explicit uniform --model/CLAUDE_MODEL, which wins over the per-agent tier default. Resolution distinguishes a user-supplied uniform model from a fallback to the default constant.

criteria.name: evaluator_ge_generator_invariant_warning
criteria.description: When the resolved configuration would place the Evaluator tier below the Generator tier, a clear HARNESS-tagged warning naming the invariant is emitted exactly once and the run is NOT hard-failed. criteria.name: model_contract_knob
criteria.description: A new optional --model-contract CLI flag plus matching MODEL_CONTRACT env var is plumbed through NegotiateContractOptions. When set, all negotiation SDK calls — proposal, review, and the F5 bounded narrowing round — use the specified model. When unset, negotiation preserves the existing inherited split (proposal on the Generator model, review and narrowing on the Evaluator model). The addition is additive and does not disturb the F5 size-limit option fields.

criteria.name: honest_startup_model_log
criteria.description: On startup, runHarness prints the resolved model for all four agents including the Documenter (which was previously omitted), reflecting the actual per-agent matrix rather than a single Model: line, in the plain HARNESS voice with each line standing alone.

criteria.name: help_documents_matrix_and_flags
criteria.description: CLI_FLAG_HELP/printHelp documents the recommended per-agent matrix, the Evaluator ≥ Generator rationale, and the new --model-contract flag (including its MODEL_CONTRACT env var). The --model help text no longer cites the stale claude-opus-4-6 default ID.

criteria.name: operational_app_starts_clean
criteria.description: The project typechecks (bun run typecheck), lints (bun run lint), and passes the full test suite (bun test) with no errors. The harness starts end-to-end with the new per-agent defaults and reaches normal operation without runtime errors.

criteria.name: test_command_detected_from_package_json
criteria.description: Given a project whose package.json scripts include a recognizable test entry (e.g. 'test', 'test:unit', 'bun test'), the detector identifies and returns the canonical test command string without throwing

criteria.name: test_command_detection_coexists_with_lint_typecheck
criteria.description: The test-command detection integrates into the same static-analysis detection path used for lint and typecheck; calling the detection function returns all three (lint, typecheck, test) when all are present, and any subset when only some are present

criteria.name: test_command_runs_exactly_once_per_attempt
criteria.description: For a given attempt, the central command-runner executes the detected test command exactly one time; subsequent accesses to the result within the same attempt reuse the captured result rather than re-executing

criteria.name: structured_result_shape_is_complete
criteria.description: The captured result object contains all required fields: overall pass/fail boolean, total test count, passing count, failing count, an array of failing test name strings, and the (possibly truncated) raw output string; numeric counts are non-negative and total equals pass plus fail

criteria.name: no_test_command_degrades_to_noop
criteria.description: Given a project with no detectable test script in package.json (or no package.json at all), the runner returns a no-op result (pass/fail null or skipped, counts zero, empty failing list) and the attempt continues without error

criteria.name: test_command_spawn_failure_degrades_gracefully
criteria.description: When the test command cannot be spawned (e.g. command not found), exits non-zero with malformed output, or throws an unhandled exception, the runner records a failed result with the error captured in the output field and does not throw or crash the enclosing attempt

criteria.name: lint_and_typecheck_pass
criteria.description: bun run lint and bun run typecheck both exit 0 with no new errors or warnings introduced by this sprint's changes

criteria.name: baseline_captured_before_generator
criteria.description: When a sprint attempt begins and a test command is detectable, a baseline VerificationResult is produced before the Generator agent is invoked. It must contain at minimum: passed, failingTests[], passCount, failCount, and output fields. The baseline must be captured strictly before any Generator-driven code change.

criteria.name: classifier_labels_pre_existing_failures
criteria.description: Given a baseline with failingTests: ['test-A', 'test-B'] and a post-Generator result with failingTests: ['test-A', 'test-B', 'test-C'], classifyFailures() returns { preExisting: ['test-A', 'test-B'], newlyIntroduced: ['test-C'] }. Tests present in both sets are always labelled pre-existing.

criteria.name: classifier_green_baseline_marks_all_new
criteria.description: Given a baseline with an empty failingTests array (all tests passing) and a post-Generator result with one or more failing tests, classifyFailures() labels every failing test as newly-introduced and none as pre-existing.

criteria.name: null_baseline_degrades_gracefully
criteria.description: When the baseline VerificationResult has passed: null (i.e. equals VERIFICATION_NO_OP, meaning no test command was found or the baseline run errored), classifyFailures() returns { preExisting: [], newlyIntroduced: [], classified: false } without throwing. The sprint attempt proceeds identically to a run with no Sprint 2 feature present.

criteria.name: classifier_is_order_independent
criteria.description: classifyFailures() produces identical output regardless of the order of test names in the baseline's failingTests array and the post-Generator failingTests array. A test present in baseline but absent from the post-run result (i.e. it was fixed) does not appear in either output set.

criteria.name: classifier_never_throws
criteria.description: classifyFailures() does not throw under any input: null or undefined baseline, null or undefined post-run result, malformed or empty failingTests arrays, or mismatched types. It returns a safe default classification result (classified: false, empty arrays) in all error cases, mirroring the never-throwing style of classifySurfaces() and buildErrorVerificationResult().

criteria.name: classifier_lives_in_shared_with_no_sdk_imports
criteria.description: The classifyFailures() function and its return type (FailureClassification or equivalent) are defined in shared/verification.ts (or a new shared/ file). The file has zero imports from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk or any harness-claude/ module. tsc --noEmit passes with no new type errors.

criteria.name: unit_tests_cover_classifier_branches
criteria.description: tests/ contains unit tests for classifyFailures() covering at minimum: (1) pre-existing + newly-introduced split, (2) empty baseline (all-new), (3) null/VERIFICATION_NO_OP baseline, (4) post-run result with no failures, (5) order-independence, and (6) a malformed input that must not throw. All tests pass under bun test.

criteria.name: backward_compatibility_with_sprint1_artifacts
criteria.description: Existing Sprint 1 exports from shared/verification.ts (VerificationResult, VERIFICATION_NO_OP, parseTestOutput, buildVerificationResult, buildErrorVerificationResult) and shared/static-analysis.ts (detectTestCommand, TEST_SCRIPT_KEYS, truncateStaticAnalysisOutput) remain importable and behaviorally unchanged. No Sprint 1 test regressions under bun test.

criteria.name: post_generator_verification_run_executes
criteria.description: After the Generator completes and before the Evaluator is invoked, the attempt loop calls the verification runner (via createVerificationRunner) exactly once per attempt and captures a VerificationResult. The run must occur on every attempt regardless of whether --test-gate is set.

criteria.name: verification_runner_error_degrades_gracefully
criteria.description: If the post-Generator verification runner throws, exits with a spawn error, or returns an error result, the harness records the failure as a VerificationResult with passed: false and a descriptive error output, does not crash the attempt loop, and proceeds to the Evaluator. An error result must NOT set classified: true and must NOT be treated as a newly-introduced failure even when --test-gate is set.

criteria.name: classify_failures_called_with_baseline
criteria.description: On every attempt where both a Sprint 2 pre-Generator baseline and a post-Generator VerificationResult are available, classifyFailures is invoked with those two inputs and its output (preExisting and newlyIntroduced sets, classified flag) is attached to the result before injection. When the baseline is absent or passed === null, classifyFailures is not called and the FailureClassification carries classified: false.

criteria.name: unclassified_baseline_does_not_trigger_gate
criteria.description: When classifyFailures returns classified: false (baseline absent, baseline passed === null, or any error in the classification path), the test gate does not trigger a skip regardless of whether --test-gate is set. The attempt proceeds to the Evaluator normally and no exception propagates out of the classification or gate-check path.

criteria.name: test_gate_skips_evaluator_on_new_failures
criteria.description: When --test-gate (or TEST_GATE env var) is set and classifyFailures reports at least one newly-introduced failure, the Evaluator is skipped using buildSkippedEvaluatorResult, the attempt is recorded as failed, and the feedback payload includes the names of the newly-failing tests. The Evaluator must not be invoked in this path.

criteria.name: test_gate_off_by_default_evaluator_still_runs
criteria.description: When --test-gate is not set (the default), a post-Generator verification result containing newly-introduced failures does NOT skip the Evaluator. The Evaluator runs and serves as the sole pass/fail gate, preserving the Evaluator-tier >= Generator-tier invariant.

criteria.name: test_gate_cost_log_message
criteria.description: Whenever the test gate causes the Evaluator to be skipped, the harness emits exactly one log line at normal level in plain English stating both what it did (skipped the Evaluator) and the cost consequence (e.g. 'Skipped Evaluator — N newly-introduced test failure(s) detected; evaluation token cost avoided.'). The count N must equal the number of newly-introduced failures, and the message style/grammar must match the existing surface-coverage and lint-gate messages in sprint-attempts.ts.

criteria.name: gate_ordering_surface_then_lint_then_test
criteria.description: The test gate is evaluated only after the surface-coverage gate and the lint gate have both passed. If either earlier gate triggers a skip, the test gate code is not reached. The ordering must be observable from the code structure in sprint-attempts.ts and documented in an inline comment.

criteria.name: test_gate_config_precedence

criteria.name: default_caps_preserve_existing_behavior

criteria.name: per_agent_cap_isolation

criteria.name: invalid_cap_degrades_to_default

criteria.name: caps_wired_to_sdk_maxturns

Verified by inspecting the value passed at the call site (unit test with a spy/mock on runAgent).

criteria.name: standard_precedence_respected
criteria.description: For each per-agent cap, the resolution order CLI flag > env var > .adhd/.env > default is enforced: a CLI flag beats a matching env var, an env var beats .adhd/.env, and .adhd/.env beats the hardcoded default. Verified by unit-testing resolveConfig with combinations of sources.

criteria.name: unit_tests_cover_resolution_paths
criteria.description: Unit tests in tests/ cover: (a) default resolution for all four agents, (b) valid CLI/env overrides for at least two agents, (c) invalid values (non-numeric, negative, zero) degrading to defaults for at least two agents, and (d) precedence ordering (CLI beats env). All tests pass under bun test with no skips.

criteria.name: harness_starts_cleanly

criteria.name: prompt_requests_partial_output

criteria.name: splice_preserves_completed_sections_verbatim

criteria.name: splice_inserts_revised_sections_in_order

criteria.name: splice_falls_back_to_original_without_throwing

criteria.name: diff_display_preserved

criteria.name: hitl_and_noninteractive_auto_accept_preserved

criteria.name: regression_preservation_preserved

criteria.name: default_behavior_unchanged_without_flag

criteria.name: unit_tests_cover_splice_logic
criteria.description: tests/ contains unit tests for spliceRefinementSections that pass under bun test, covering at minimum: correct assembly from completed + revised sections, byte-exact completed-section preservation, the sprint-count-preserving ordinal insertion, and the fallback path returning the original spec unchanged on missing/unresolvable headers without throwing

criteria.name: parse_approved_envelope
criteria.description: parseReviewEnvelope given { verdict: 'APPROVED', changes: '' } returns a result indicating approval with no contract override, so the caller uses the proposal text as the contract source — identical outcome to the former APPROVED string branch

criteria.name: parse_revised_envelope
criteria.description: parseReviewEnvelope given { verdict: 'REVISED', changes: 'Changed threshold for foo from 6 to 8', contract: { ... } } returns verdict=revised and the contract object from the envelope as the selected contract source

criteria.name: parse_legacy_approved_string
criteria.description: parseReviewEnvelope given the trimmed literal string 'APPROVED' returns verdict=approved — preserving backward compatibility with existing reviewer responses that predate the envelope format

criteria.name: parse_legacy_bare_contract
criteria.description: parseReviewEnvelope given a raw contract JSON string with no verdict field returns verdict=revised and the parsed contract object, preserving backward compatibility with the existing raw-contract path that feeds parseContract in negotiateContract

criteria.name: parse_envelope_never_throws
criteria.description: parseReviewEnvelope returns a defined fallback result (treating the input as a bare contract or signaling parse failure) for any malformed, empty, non-JSON, or structurally unexpected input — it never throws and never crashes the run, matching the never-throwing style of shared/contract-limits.ts and shared/verification.ts

criteria.name: negotiate_contract_uses_envelope_parser
criteria.description: negotiateContract selects the contract source via parseReviewEnvelope rather than the former literal string comparison (contractSource = reviewText.trim() === 'APPROVED' ? proposalText : reviewText); for both legacy input forms and the new envelope, the selected contract is identical to what the old branch would have chosen

criteria.name: narrowing_round_uses_envelope_parser

criteria.name: contract_marker_retirement_removes_criterion

criteria.name: retirement_durability_blocks_resurrection
criteria.description: Given a criterion that was retired in sprint N, when a subsequent sprint N+1 accumulates a new behavioral criterion with the exact same name, then the durable retired-names set prevents that name from appearing in the persisted suite — the newer criterion is silently dropped rather than resurrecting the retired entry.

criteria.name: retired_criteria_absent_from_evaluator_section
criteria.description: Given a suite that contains a retired criterion, when `buildRegressionSection` is called for any later sprint, then the retired criterion's name and description do not appear anywhere in the returned section string.

criteria.name: legacy_bare_array_loads_without_error
criteria.description: Given an existing `regression.json` file whose content is a bare JSON array of `{ name, description, threshold, sprintNumber }` objects with no tier, surfaces, or retired-names fields, when `readRegressionCriteria` reads it, then it returns a valid array of criteria with no thrown exception and no loss of existing entries.

criteria.name: new_fields_round_trip_correctly
criteria.description: Given criteria accumulated with tier and surfaces fields plus a non-empty retired-names set, when the store is written to `regression.json` and then read back by `readRegressionCriteria`, then the tier, surfaces, and retired-names values are byte-for-byte identical to what was written — no field is dropped, coerced, reordered, or silently defaulted.

criteria.name: legacy_criteria_always_checked
criteria.description: Given criteria in the suite that have no tier or surfaces field (legacy shape), when `buildRegressionSection` is called for a sprint touching any surface set, then all such criteria are included in the returned section regardless of surface matching — they are never omitted by the relevance filter.

criteria.name: core_criteria_always_checked

criteria.name: surface_relevance_filter_excludes_non_matching

criteria.name: regression_section_size_bounded
criteria.description: Given a suite of 50 behavioral criteria all tagged 'optional' with surfaces disjoint from the current sprint, when `buildRegressionSection` is called, then the returned string's character count is less than or equal to its character count when called with 100 such criteria, and that count stays under a fixed documented upper bound — the section size does not grow linearly with suite count.

criteria.name: non_coding_agent_no_mcp

criteria.name: coding_agent_tool_retention

criteria.name: mcp_disable_override_precedence

criteria.name: budget_80pct_single_warning

criteria.name: budget_100pct_interactive_pause

criteria.name: budget_100pct_noninteractive_continue
criteria.description: When a per-sprint token budget is reached in non-interactive mode (no TTY / CI environment), the harness does not pause or call promptGate; instead it logs a single one-line HARNESS warning stating the overage and auto-continues — matching the non-interactive policy already established by other gates.

criteria.name: budget_inert_when_unset

criteria.name: pure_decision_returns_success_on_valid_json

criteria.name: all_existing_parse_strategies_preserved

criteria.name: preview_is_bounded
criteria.description: The bounded preview in the failure result is never longer than 200 characters regardless of the length of the raw input; unit tests confirm this for (a) a 10 000-character invalid input, (b) an empty string, and (c) an input shorter than 200 characters which must be returned in full and never truncated

criteria.name: failure_result_contains_valid_default_contract

criteria.name: suite_stays_green

criteria.name: wrapper_public_signature_unchanged

criteria.name: parse_failure_emits_warning_not_error
